title: Me gustaría vivir allí
blurbEn: The conditional: what would happen, and the politest way to ask for anything in Spanish.
body:
Me gustaría vivir en México algún día.

No sé si sería fácil. Echaría de menos a mi familia, la comida de mi madre y las calles de Madrid. Pero creo que aprendería muchísimo.

Viviría en una casa pequeña, cerca del mar. Trabajaría por la mañana y estudiaría por la tarde. Los fines de semana viajaría a los pueblos pequeños y conocería a gente de todo el país.

Sería una vida más lenta y más tranquila, con menos ruido y menos prisa.

Podría escribir un blog sobre la experiencia.

Mi madre dice que yo no aguantaría ni tres meses lejos de casa. Probablemente tiene razón. Pero me gustaría intentarlo.
translationEn:
I'd like to live in Mexico one day.

I don't know if it would be easy. I would miss my family, my mother's cooking and the streets of Madrid. But I think I would learn an enormous amount.

I would live in a small house, near the sea. I would work in the morning and study in the afternoon. At weekends I would travel to the small villages and meet people from all over the country.

It would be a slower, quieter life, with less noise and less hurry.

I could write a blog about the experience.

My mother says I wouldn't last even three months away from home. She's probably right. But I'd like to try.

gustaría.note: You have been using this since Unit 5. It is the conditional of 'gustar', and it is softer and more polite than 'me gusta'.

sería.note: Same stem as the future ('será'), different endings — the conditional uses the imperfecto endings -ía, -ías, -ía.

phrases.note: 'echar de menos' is the Spanish for missing someone. Literally 'to throw of less', which helps nobody — learn it whole.
